findings.title: Relation rung ladder not carried by the registry the identity contract names
findings.chosenLaw: x-opensip-relation-registry gains an explicit ordered `ladder` (weakest-first, inherited verbatim from fact-plane relationRegistry plus [observed] for unresolved-edge) and is the SINGLE authority. `rungs` keeps its real meaning as the per-rung field-rule table; an empty table is never an absent ladder. Membership is against `ladder` always, with no empty-ladder fallback. Order is the index within one relation's ladder; no global rank; cross-relation comparison is an admission refusal.
findings.evidenceBefore: probes/p2b_rung_exploit.py: DEFECT-PRESENT with a passing positive control - a `declares` fact carrying resolved-callee/checked/resolved-binding/resolved-target/normalized-body-hash closes a Run on frozen bytes.
findings.evidenceAfter: CLOSED; all five refuse RELATION_RUNG_NOT_IN_LADDER; positive control still closes.

findings.title: RELATION-LADDER-DOMAIN-V2.ladders alphabetised while declaring the inherited ladder as its source
findings.detail: calls/imports/references were REVERSED relative to the ladder they name. Harmless only because that registry is consulted for membership alone; anything reading it as an order would let a syntactic fact satisfy a demand for a resolved rung. Reordered weakest-first; membership unchanged.

findings.title: minResolution carries two disjoint closed vocabularies with no published mapping
findings.optionsWeighed: Abstract syntax plus a complete normative mapping was rejected: the mapping must be per relation (`resolved` names a different rung in imports/references/calls/reachability, `type` only for types, `external` no native rung), so it is a partial lossy renaming with no expressive power, it does not preserve one-word-one-meaning, and `syntax<resolved<type` IS a global ladder that dissolves into rung names once made relation-relative. It would also ADD a mostly-empty normative table while RES_ORDER had to die either way.
findings.chosenLaw: Atom.minResolution and repair EvidenceRequirement.minResolution are RUNG names. The abstract Resolution enum and the global RES_ORDER rank are withdrawn. Satisfaction is ladder-index comparison inside one relation. Schema constrains the flat vocabulary (necessary only, drift-checked as the union of the authority's ladders); ladder membership is enforced at admission in resolve_policy, in repair_preview, and AT THE RUN CLOSURE over both PolicyDocumentV1 and the compiled RuleProgramV1.
findings.closedRelationNamespace: An atom names a native fact relation or an imported-evidence relation from the new imported-evidence#/x-opensip-evidence-relation-registry (runtime-observation, history-change; one-rung ladder [observed] - no new rung token, `observed` is already unresolved-edge's rung). Evidence relations must declare their evidence kind; native fact relations must not carry one.
findings.compatibility: Dialect change to PolicyDocumentV1/RuleProgramV1/PolicyTestSuiteV1/repair EvidenceRequirement. Design-stage: all 28 in-kit instances rewritten by an explicit per-relation table that refuses to guess. Every rewrite preserves ladder position, so no expected verdict changes. A policy outside this kit needs the same per-relation migration; there is no compatible global rewrite, which is itself evidence the abstract tier was never well-defined.
findings.preserved: Strong-Kleene evaluation, all-covered, Coverage sufficiency and universal-negative requirements unchanged. No global boolean replaces Coverage sufficiency. The small fixture interpreter is still not a production evaluator.
findings.independentConfirmation: Reverting only subject bytes under corrected fixtures reproduces RES_ORDER[f['resolution']] -> KeyError: 'resolved-target', matching root's own frozen-v12 probe.

findings.title: syntax-only has SUPPORTED-DESIGN fact cells but no admissible universe value
findings.chosenLaw: Third registered universe native.semantic-universe.syntax.v2 over context native.context.syntax.v2. Context carries only a closure-bound SyntaxGrammarBundleV1 (kind=grammar closure, parserVersion from the closure manifest, every grammar/bundle/normalizer digest in the retained tree). Universe commits the admitted context plus the SELECTED grammar set and the constant resolutionAttempted=false. body-language-version.dialect gains a {grammarVariant} branch so a grammar parse never mints the same identity as a compiler parse.
findings.rejected: Nullable universe fields (deletes the invariant that every fact states what produced it) and narrowing the matrix (removes advertised capability, explicitly forbidden).
findings.capabilityNotWidened: Only inventory, syntactic and clones rungs. Semantic rungs stay language-tier-unsupported, unresolved-edge unavailable, universal negatives still require complete Coverage.
findings.existingJoinRespected: Bundled grammar languageIds are held EQUAL to the closed body-language-version languageId enum by an executed drift check, so advertised grammar coverage cannot outrun what a clone identity can express.
findings.evidenceAfter: A real syntax-only Run closes end to end; file/package/vcs-change inventory Runs close; a clones fact over a .rs body closes with no Cargo, no edition and no ownership record; 13 discriminating controls (missing context, wrong context language, foreign context bytes, absent grammar in selection, version not from manifest, digests not in the retained closure, ambiguous suffix, unretained closure, cross-universe same-only, both wrong-domain frame directions).

findings.title: ScopeDocumentV1 required as an analysis-spec parameter, closed registry has no row

No arbitrary registeredSchemas fallback and no permissive unregistered parameter.
findings.hardening: The class is keyed by DOCUMENT digest, so two rows over one document would be indistinguishable and the first listed would silently win. An ambiguous key now refuses (PAYLOAD_PARAMETER_AMBIGUOUS_ROW).

findings.title: Partial-ownership Coverage disclosure has no publishable typed cause
findings.chosenLaw: NativeCause gains body-language-ownership-missing / body-language-owner-unenumerated / body-language-owner-ambiguous, mapped in the section 10 input-closure-incomplete row. The other selection-law refusals get no cause, explicitly justified: OWNER_NOT_COMPILED/OWNER_NOT_SELECTED are per-body refusals section 11 states are compatible with coverage=complete; DIALECT_ABSENT/AMBIGUOUS refuse before a Coverage entry exists.
findings.note: A nullable nativeCause does not fulfil a mandated disclosure; a null records that one was owed and not made. Body refusal and indeterminate empty-clones Coverage unchanged.

findings.title: import.blobs cardinality diverges (zero AND more than 4096)
findings.chosenLaw: minItems 1 decided from required payload/closure semantics, not strictness: blobs is the closed inventory of retained artifact members and adapterClosure asserts an adapter ran over the bytes sourcePath names, so a zero-blob import claims a payload whose inputs were never retained and whose payloadDigest can never be re-derived. maxItems 4096 and the item byte bound are the import unit's own published hostile-input bounds, carried as a distinct foundation `import-blob` record so they are not imposed on source-inventory or closure tree rows.
findings.intentionalAdmissibilityChange: The foundation harness graph_with_import() built blobs=[]; that was this divergence in the candidate's own corpus (the same wrapper would have been refused by the mirror), not intentional admissibility. It now names the artifact it read.
findings.preimagesUnaffected: Registered preimages remain a separate, fully joined and required set (retainedPreimages), unchanged.
